target_customer: Cricket and insect farmers (yield tools) and later buyers of live feeder insects and pet food ingredients
problem: Labor is about 75 percent of cricket farm costs, so tools that standardize egg volume and other husbandry steps could cut costs.
business_model: Farm tooling at launch; later operating its own insect farms and selling live feeder insects

founders.name: Trina Chiasson
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page. TechCrunch says she ran a small experiment selling edible insects.

founders.name: James Ricci
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/CTO on the YC page and named co-founder by TechCrunch.

founders.name: Teq Sassmannshaus
founders.background_notes: Described as biotech hardware engineer co-founder in the YC description; no founder profile on the YC page.

competitors.name: Aspire Food Group
competitors.what: Cricket farming and protein, which acquired the cricket bar brand Exo in March 2018 and ran an automated cricket farm
competitors.traction_then: Consolidating cricket supply and food brands

technical_complexity.rationale: Biological husbandry plus automation hardware on a farm. Hard because of live insect variability, but built with known sensors and handling equipment.

defensibility.rationale: Know how of husbandry and a farm site help, but a larger entrenched cricket producer could copy tooling.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch in March 2018 noted larger businesses could target the space; the same month Aspire bought Exo. No evidence of direct copying of Ovipost.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (March 2018) cited labor at about 75 percent of farm costs and growing interest in cricket protein. Demand for insect protein in feed was still early.

identity.voice_and_tone: Current site speaks as a team of farmers, entomologists, engineers and entrepreneurs focused on clean, chemical free farming.

branding.community_and_virality: A Science News piece describes a demo day moment with a snow globe of a million cricket eggs; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Some press (TechCrunch, Science News) but little brand specific coverage and no sourced name story.

pivots.from: Software and tooling for cricket farmers
pivots.to: Operating its own insect farms and selling live insects
pivots.why: Science News says the team bought an older cricket farm in LaBelle, Florida; the reason is not stated in the source seen.

outcome_analysis: Ovipost launched from Winter 2018 with tools for cricket farmers, then bought a Florida cricket farm and moved into producing insects itself. The YC directory marks it Inactive, yet ovipost.com currently sells live feeder insects, so the company may still operate under the name. No shutdown cause is public, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: Funding rests on databases only: CB Insights reports 320K total and PitchBook reports 120K total, with different investor lists (PitchBook also lists Azolla Ventures and BoxOne Ventures). No round dates or amounts per round were found, and the round recorded rests on a single database. Status conflict: YC lists Inactive but the website is live with a 2026 copyright. Exit type left unknown for that reason. Competitor Aspire source is dated within the batch month; the competitor list is otherwise empty because no other dated sources were found.
